reviews.title: Worth the hype
reviews.body: I was skeptical that the KitchenAid was worth the hype, but I was wrong. It is a marvel of engineering, heavyweight, easy to operate, and super easy to clean. I wanted it in this shade of red, which perfectly matches the other touches of red in my kitchen. My baking game has improved by leaps and strides, especially pound cakes, which I make frequently. I don’t even put it up, but leave it on the counter.

reviews.title: Love my KitchenAid
reviews.body: Who wouldn’t love a KitchenAid?!  My old one finally bit the dust after 35 years so I purchased this new one.  I tried the bigger one where the bowl lifts up and down and hated it.  Nothing wrong with it, but I just am so used to this particular model.  Love it and all of its’ attachments. And of course the quality of a KitchenAid is always great.

reviews.title: High value bundle!
reviews.body: I'm not going to review the Kitchenaide Artisan here, simply this color and bundle.  Bought it during Amazon Days at an attractive price (thanks Amazon) and it included the flex-edge beater, a must have for these mixers IMO, increasing the value here.  The Gloss Black color is a great choice as it is easy to see dirt and keep clean too, unlike some of the pastel, metallic or white color ways.

reviews.title: Feeling a little cheated
reviews.body: I recently purchased this stand mixer and love it. One of the reasons I bought it was because of all the attachments included. Item description (and rufus) said it comes with a pouring shield. MIne did not. I contacted KitchenAid directly and they said a shield is NOT included in this bundle. Amazon said it is supposed to have a shield. Hmmmm. They said I could replace it but it's very heavy and I don't want to go thru the hassle of returning it AND possibly get another without the shield. I ordered a shield thru KitchenAid for $25!!! I will eat the $ as opposed to the return process but can't help but feel I've been a little cheated.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 2, 2026
reviews.author: Fluffy

reviews.title: Can't believe that I waited so long.
reviews.body: I have wanted a Kitchen Aid mixer for at least 30 years and have always put it off because I couldn't justify the price.  Now that I finally broke down and bought one, I see why they are so expensive.  I was shocked at how quickly it creamed butter and sugar with no effort whatsoever.  This is a relatively quiet mixer compared to my Sunbeam.  The Sunbeam was adequate, but I was never quite satisfied.  I love watching some of the baking shows and, of course, they are all using Kitchen Aid mixers, so I finally bought this one.  If you are taken aback by the price, please remember that you get what you pay for and this is a machine well worth the cost.  The only drawback (which is probably one of the reasons it is so good) is the weight, it's pretty heavy.  Mine did come with two small scratches that were down to the metal and they weren't due from shipping.  The other drawback is that I will gain at least a million pounds from making cakes and such, because it's so much fun to use.  Buy one, you won't regret it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 26, 2020
reviews.author: sandra

features: Included Flex Edge Beater reduces mixing time and the need to scrape ingredients down the side of the bowl
Built to take it all on with the durable and built-to-last metal construction, and 59 touchpoints around the mixer bowl for great mixing results.
5 Quart Stainless Steel Bowl with comfortable handle for small or large batches, to mix up 9 dozen cookies* in a single batch. Dishwasher safe. *Using the flat beater; 28g dough each.
Easily add ingredients with the tilt-head design, because you'll have better access to the bowl - lock the head in place while mixing
10 speeds for nearly any task or recipe, from mixing ingredients together on the stir speed, to whipping cream at speed 8, you'll get thorough ingredient incorporation every time
